newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil ends tax-free capital goods imports - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil ends tax-free capital goods imports - report.

text.p: The Brazilian government Friday published a decree which news agencies said ended tax exemption on imports of nearly 3,700 items, in particular capital goods.
Private Invest News agency said the items would now be subject to a 17 percent import tax, up from zero.

Quoting Frederico Alvarez, executive secretary of the Council of Foreign Trade in Brasilia, Invest News said telecommunications components would continue to be tax free until the end of the year, a decision he described as "political" because of the ongoing privatization of Brazil's telecommunications sector.
Alvares could not be reached for comment and no one was immediately available at the Finance Ministry, which drew up the decree in conjunction with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
Alvares said the tax exemption list for imports would be discontinued because the measure had achieved its objective of encouraging capital goods imports.

Capital goods imports, including factory machinery and trucks, have been identified by government officials as the villain behind the burgeoning trade gap, already running at over $4.7 billion this year after $5.5 billion in the whole of 1996.
But Alvares noted that the tax free list encompassed only 15 percent of all capital goods imports.
